history.summary: Hindu Shiva temple on the south bank of the Narmada, on the mainland opposite the Omkareshwar island shrine (RELATED RECORD: seq 1811). Considered the 'other half' of the 4th Jyotirlinga — the Dwadash Jyotirling Stotra tradition treats both shrines as one manifestation, and pilgrims are advised to visit Mamleshwar first. The ASI-maintained complex holds a black, smooth Shivalinga with Parvati behind it, smaller shrines to Parvati, Ganesha and Kartikeya, a Nandi mandapa, and Mahimna Stotram inscriptions on the walls; a small three-sided mosque stands toward the west. Daily lingarchan rituals here are traced to the reign of Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar (22 brahmins then, 5 now). Believers hold that Shiva comes here each night after his rounds, and the priests perform a secret Shayan Aarti at 8:30 PM — though the Shayan Aarti is more commonly attributed to the island temple, so this claim is UNVERIFIED (verify). Coordinates are APPROXIMATE: the geocoder did not resolve the mainland temple separately, so they are estimated from its documented position on the south bank opposite the Omkareshwar island temple (22.24587, 76.15077).

name: Mamleshwar (Amareshwar) Temple
town_description: Omkareshwar is a small pilgrimage town in Khandwa district built around the Om-shaped Mandhata Island in the Narmada river, site of one of the twelve Jyotirlingas. A bridge connects the mainland to the island, and a 7-8 km parikrama path circles the island past many small shrines. The Mamleshwar temple stands on the mainland south bank near Gomukh Ghat, reached from the island by a hanging bridge or a short boat ride. It is about 77 km from Indore, the usual gateway.

travel.airport: Devi Ahilyabai Holkar Airport, Indore, ~77 km
travel.railway: Omkareshwar Road station ~12 km; Khandwa ~72 km
travel.road: Regular buses/taxis from Indore, Ujjain and Bhopal; local auto/boat to cross the Narmada to the island shrine

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivratri (Feb) for the grandest celebrations
